newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends mostly up on short-covering.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends mostly up on short-covering.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended mostly up on Tuesday due to short-covering ahead of the Christmas holiday despite overnight losses on the London Metal Exchange, traders said.
The most active April 1997 contract ended at 20,440 yuan ($2,463) per tonne, rising 70 yuan. It opened at an intra-day low of 20,220 and hit a high of 20,450.
January was unchanged at 20,200, February fell 20 to 20,300, March rose 50 to 20,390, May 60 to 20,440 and June 60 to 20,460.
Combined volume rose to 62,650 tonnes from 39,390.
Copper opened lower. Short-covering dominated today's trading and pushed prices up, with many investors liquidating their long positions at high levels.
"Long and short position holders wanted to liquidate their positions due to the uncertain short-term market trend," one trader said.
"But the firmer spot copper price supported the confidence of long position holders," he added. In Shanghai, the current spot copper price is around 20,200 yuan per tonne.
Traders said the second reason for today's short-covering was that investors did not want to hold positions ahead of the year-end.
"World metal markets will suspend trading for two days during the Christmas holiday, so wary investors preferred to take a wait-and-see attitude," a second trader said.
Analysts expect copper to stay between 20,000 and 20,500 in the next few days.
Aluminium ended down. The only traded January contract ended at 13,850 yuan per tonne, losing 50 yuan, in thin volume of 20 tonnes. ($1=8.2983 yuan)
